subject: Urgent: p99 latency & error burst after model upgrade
messages:
From: Aisha Khan <aisha.khan@sonnetfin.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.example.com
Cc: Ryan Cole <ryan.cole@sonnetfin.com>
Date: 2028-04-27T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Spike in p99 & errors after model upgrade

Hi Karthik,

We started seeing a sharp increase in p99 latency and a spike in 502/503 errors right after your team flipped to v3.1 + quant-high last night. Impact window: ~02:40–09:00 PDT. Our user-facing latency p99 doubled and throughput for the payments flow dropped ~35%.

Attached are our aggregated p99 traces and a screenshot of the 502s from our gateway. Sample observations:
- 502s cluster around long decode stalls (stack traces attached).
- Error rate concentrated on requests >1k tokens and on the /v1/complete endpoint.
- We saw several retries from the client which compounded load.

We need an immediate rollback or a routing to the previous variant. Can you confirm you can revert to v3.0 or route Sonnet to the stable model within the hour? This is affecting live payments — CTO loop is on standby.

Thanks,
Aisha Khan
Head of Platform Reliability, Sonnet Financial
--
Aisha Khan
Sonnet Financial
attachments: sonnet-p99-logs-0427.csv, screenshot-error-502.png
From: karthik_iyer@redwood.example.com
To: Aisha Khan <aisha.khan@sonnetfin.com>

Date: 2028-04-27T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Spike in p99 & errors after model upgrade

Aisha — thanks for the quick heads-up and the logs. Really sorry you're seeing this. We're treating it as P1.

Plan (short):
1) Immediate: we can route Sonnet traffic to the last stable variant (v3.0 / quant-standard) within ~20–30 minutes. Need your approval to trigger failover now.
2) Triage: infra will pull decoder logs and telemetry to confirm whether the issue is in kernel path (quant-high) or NVDecode stalls.
3) Post-mortem: we'll share a timeline and corrective actions (changes to canary thresholds and qprofile gating).

If you approve rollback, we'll start the routing change and open a shared bridge. Proposed bridge: 10:30 PT. Please confirm.

—Karthik

From: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.example.com

Date: 2028-04-27T10:07:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Spike in p99 & errors after model upgrade

Karthik / team — quick triage notes from runtime:
- Canary telemetry shows decoder stalls and a rise in tokenization time for long sequences after the v3.1 quant-high push.
- Error 502s correspond to AVX kernel fallbacks we saw on some older nodes; those nodes were part of the burst pool serving Sonnet.
- Memory footprint increased ~12% on quant-high for certain prompt shapes which triggered GC/eviction chatter.

Immediate mitigations I recommend (in order):
1) Route Sonnet to v3.0+quant-standard (fastest, lowest risk).
2) Remove the older nodes from the burst pool temporarily (they're tripping on kernel fallback).
3) Apply a temporary per-client max tokens cap (1500) to reduce long-tail requests.

I can implement 1+2 immediately if ops approves the routing change. We'll capture metrics pre/post to validate.

Stephanie Nguyen
SRE Lead, Runtime
Redwood Inference

Looping in leadership per SLA risk. I'm drafting a short exec note for the CTO at Sonnet and our VP Eng (for transparency). TL;DR: we will perform an emergency routing rollback to v3.0 quant-standard and pause quant-high canaries for 24h.

Mitigation ETA and customer impact:
- Authorization to rollback now -> start in ~20 mins, expected full routing complete in 30–45 mins.
- Expected p99 improvement: ~30–45% in early estimates (based on canary metrics).
- We'll issue a credit/waiver for the incident window pending post-mortem.

Action items for execs:
- Approve rollback and customer credit (small discretionary credit ok).
- Approve short-term pause of quant-high rollout and a retrofitted canary gate for long-tail prompts.

I'll prepare the exec note and join any customer bridge.

Rishi Malhotra
VP, Post-Deploy Reliability
Redwood Inference
